releases.name: rolebox v2.3.0
releases.body:
2.3.0 adds native Codex roles and managed graph execution, moves the dsh monitor and logs into conversation views, and removes the wall-clock limit from team turns. Public Codex roles become native agents while their private children stay scoped, the MCP runtime supplies six session tools and five graph tools, and managed workers submit through the shared acceptance ledger while running native tools inside the host's sandbox. On dsh, Rolebox and Logs mount beside Chat and Trajectory, `/rolebox/status` scopes loops and engine graphs to the session, team tools return compact receipts, and `graph_status` discloses node prompts only on request. The release also lets any active member resume a paused team, reports an incomplete TUI session scope and follows depth-2+ dispatch chains, repairs malformed dsh outcome submissions in the same worker turn, keys the log follower by exact file identity, and composes team peers through the host gateway seams. Test hardening for the log-rotation and browser-navigation races is included. The behavior changes an existing declaration or automation may notice — including the Codex sync and restart — are recorded under Upgrade Notes.

### Upgrade Notes

- **`graph_status` omits node prompts unless `include_prompt: true`** — summary, tree and historic run output no longer carry prompt bodies by default, so status payloads and exports shrink; the option is accepted for summary, tree and json output. `query` still matches stored prompts, and declarations, worker delivery and audit records are unchanged. A caller that read a prompt from a status payload must pass the new argument. Reference: [docs/graph-outcome-protocol.md](docs/graph-outcome-protocol.md).

- **`team_create` and `team_send_event` return compact receipts instead of echoing their input** — creation reports the team and member identities, status and turn budget without the submitted goal or event history; sending reports the event id, sequence, type, sender, resolved recipient, task id, timestamp and effective wake flag without the content. The goal and event bodies stay durable and are read with `team_status(team_id?, after_seq?)`, and a receipt does not mean a peer started or finished its turn. Automation that parsed the echoed goal or content from a tool result must read it from `team_status`. Reference: [docs/team-work.md](docs/team-work.md).

- **Codex users must re-run `rolebox sync codex`, run `codex plugin add rolebox@rolebox`, and restart Codex** — sync now writes a native agent file for every public role and regenerates the plugin bundle; the MCP server launched by that bundle now exposes the six session tools and five graph tools. The plugin command installs or refreshes Codex's local cache, and Codex discovers the new agents and MCP surface only after a restart. Private children are not exported as native agents. A project's roles generate agents under `.codex/agents` when the MCP server boots and need a restart after that. Reference: [docs/codex.md](docs/codex.md).

### Features

- **Codex gains native roles, session tools and managed graph execution** — `rolebox sync codex` writes a `rolebox--<role>` native agent TOML for every public role and fingerprints the managed files so later syncs update or remove only owned content, while a project's roles are exported to `.codex/agents` when the MCP server boots; private children stay runtime descriptors, excluded from native discovery and launchable only by their owning role through `graph_declare`. The MCP server registers the six session tools (`session_list`, `session_read`, `session_search`, `session_info`, `session_diff`, `session_fork`) over native app-server threads and the five graph tools (`graph_declare`, `graph_submit_outcome`, `graph_status`, `graph_audit`, `graph_control`); managed workers are app-server threads that settle through the shared ledger and acceptance gates, and their file, shell and other task work runs through native Codex tools inside the inherited sa

releases.name: rolebox v2.2.0
releases.body:
2.2.0 makes graph workers use the declaring session's capabilities directly: they inherit the parent's authorized task tools with native schemas by default, load references through the same role-scoped loader as skills, receive each node's outcome contract on every dispatch, and get turn recall and session focus when their memory tools are authorized. On dsh, workers now run commands and file operations through the host's own tools — rolebox's `graph_worker_exec` runner, its sandbox seam and the per-attempt resource copy are gone — and the worker's role text moves into one agent-scoped system section. The release also ships the packaged `rolebox-config` skill, adds window targeting and geometry-verified image-pixel mapping to the `computer_*` family, fixes the dsh presentation-metadata and teammate-cleanup failures and classifies `browse_eval` page errors, and speeds up hashline reads and edits. The two behavior changes an existing declaration or automation may notice are recorded under Upgrade Notes.

### Upgrade Notes

- **A graph node's `tools` list no longer restricts worker task tools** — the declaration still parses, but a list, including `tools: []`, is accepted as legacy metadata that neither restricts, grants nor registers anything. Every worker now inherits the parent session's authorized task tools and exposes their native schemas; parent permissions, role policy, host registration, approval handling and the execution guard still apply, and discovery or code presentation remains opt-in. A declaration that used a list to withhold a tool must express that restriction in the parent or role policy instead. Reference: [docs/worker-tools.md](docs/worker-tools.md).

- **dsh graph workers run commands, file operations, builds and tests through the host's native tools, and `graph_worker_exec` is removed** — the host's native command and file tools (for example `bash`) now carry the command surface, with the host owning the environment, working directory, sandbox policy, approvals, timeout and cancellation; the disposable environment that hid credentials and host state is gone. Role skills and references are no longer copied into a per-attempt private directory and load through `load_role_skill` and `load_reference` at their original paths. A worker keeps `graph_submit_outcome` alongside the parent-authorized native tools. A prompt or workflow that called `graph_worker_exec` must name the host's command tool instead. Reference: [docs/graph-outcome-protocol.md](docs/graph-outcome-protocol.md); [docs/worker-tools.md](docs/worker-tools.md).

### Features

- **Graph workers inherit the parent's authorized task tools and load references by exact name** — an omitted `tools` list used to inherit the catalog while `tools: []` withheld every additional task tool; both now resolve to the parent's authorization, and the worker's default presentation exposes the inherited native schemas rather than a discovery surface. `load_reference({ name })` loads a role, skill or visible nested sub-agent reference with the same visibility as `load_role_skill`, returns its full content and resolved path, lists only visible names on a miss, and prefers deeper sub-agent resources on a name collision; skill and reference listings now name their loader and search fallback, and prompts direct agents to the loaders instead of reading private copies through a command tool. `native`, `discover` and `code` presentation remain available explicitly, with up to 32 preloaded exact names. Reference: [docs/worker-tools.md](docs/worker-tools.md); [docs/references.md](docs/references.md#loading-references).

- **Every graph dispatch carries the node's compiled outcome contract** — DSH, Pi and OpenCode 1/2 deliver the node's outcomes, each outcome's optional `data.schema` identity and exact version, its ordered acceptance gates and the declared completion policy in the attempt handoff. The runtime reads the contract from the immutable plan on initial, successor, retr

releases.name: rolebox v2.0.0
releases.body:
2.0.0 is the first stable release of the 2.x line. The breaking changes an upgrader from 1.x must act on are recorded under `## 2.0.0-alpha.1` and `## 2.0.0-alpha.2`, and are not repeated here.

### Features

- **The desktop computer-use family gains the observation and gesture tools it was missing** — the family shipped screenshot, windows, click, move, type, key and permissions; this completes the twelve-tool surface the documentation now describes with `computer_displays` (each display's screenshot id, absolute screen-coordinate bounds, `scale` and `primary`, which is what makes a capture's screen origin knowable before converting image pixels to input coordinates), `computer_focus` (bring one `computer_windows` id to the foreground and confirm the OS actually focused it, refusing when the id cannot be matched unambiguously), `computer_scroll` (one to a hundred wheel ticks in a named direction, optionally after moving the pointer first), `computer_drag` (a left-button drag between two absolute positions over a bounded duration, with a best-effort mouse-release cleanup when the gesture is interrupted) and `computer_status` (plan every operation and report the platform, helper availability, refusals, the input grant and the screen-capture grant without taking a screenshot or injecting input). On macOS every pointer, text, scroll and drag gesture is now a native Quartz event posted through JXA: `computer_click` sends real left, right and middle mouse events instead of driving System Events plus the external `cliclick` helper, `computer_type` sends Quartz Unicode keyboard events, and `computer_focus` matches the window server's identity to one unambiguous Accessibility window — so `cliclick` is no longer required and its install hint is gone. Every tool also accepts `timeout_ms` (up to two minutes) on top of a queue that serializes operations within the host process, and the live-desktop checks stay opt-in — the native macOS capture tests run only under `ROLEBOX_CUA_NATIVE_TESTS=1`, with a fixture-app smoke runner under `scripts/` — while the rewritten [docs/computer-use.md](docs/computer-use.md) documents the enablement gate, the arguments, the coordinate conversion and the per-platform limits.

- **The dsh Rolebox monitor draws an engine graph as a real node-and-edge figure** — the pane rendered every engine graph as a strip of one small cell per node, which read as a single bar and said nothing about how nodes route to each other. A graph whose `GET /rolebox/status` payload carries its version-3 declaration now renders an orthogonal layered figure: nodes are boxes in rank rows, edges are orthogonal polylines with per-edge ports so two runs can never overlap, rank-skipping edges take a right rail, back edges become a U hairpin below the rank row, declared loop groups are drawn as labelled bands, and an outcome chip appears only where the source declares two or more outcomes or the edge is a back edge. Ranks come from the strongly-connected-component condensation, so a cycle shares one rank and can neither inflate the layout nor make it recurse, and the whole layout is a pure browser-safe function (`layoutGraphTopology`, `src/platform/adapters/dsh/web-ui/graph-topology.ts`) with no DOM, clock or randomness. The figure is a single image with an accessible name and a per-node title, beside a screen-reader-only routing list that states every edge in words; a rank wider than the docked sidebar scrolls inside the canvas instead of being squeezed, and a payload with no declaration nodes keeps the strip as its fallback.

### Bug Fixes

- **A capture now checks the Screen Recording grant, and macOS input no longer breaks on the Accessibility prompt** — `computer_screenshot` captured regardless of permission, so a host without the Screen Recording grant returned a wallpaper-only PNG as if it were a screenshot; the tool now runs the `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess` probe first and refuses with the grant to enable, `computer_permissions

releases.name: rolebox v2.0.0-alpha.1
releases.body:
### Breaking Changes

- **Declared outcome graphs replace the legacy graph executor** — graph declarations now use the version-3 outcome protocol and its `graph_declare`, `graph_submit_outcome`, `graph_status`, `graph_audit` and `graph_control` tool face. Legacy graph declarations, persisted v2 execution state, the incremental node and edge construction tools, and signal-driven settlement are no longer read or run. Existing graph authors must rewrite declarations for the version-3 grammar and start new runs; the old state has no automatic migration. See [docs/graph-outcome-protocol.md](docs/graph-outcome-protocol.md) and [docs/graph-v3-operations.md](docs/graph-v3-operations.md).

- **Diagnostics moved to a typed logging platform, and the log files changed shape** — every diagnostic rolebox produces now travels one pipeline (`src/log/**`): a record carries its level, its channel, an optional registered event code, the ambient scope (session / agent / graph / run / node / attempt / effect / tool), the caller's id-state-reason-count fields and the process identity, and the sinks behind it are the console, one JSON-lines file per channel and an in-memory ring buffer. Three things an operator can see change. **File records are flat**: `{"time":…,"level":"warn","channel":"graph:host","code":"watch.settlement-threw","message":…,"scope":{…},"fields":{…},"process":{"pid":…,"role":"host"}}`, where the retired logger nested the message under `"0"` and the fields under `"1"`, so a `jq '.["1"].x'` recipe becomes `jq '.fields.x'`. **`warn` and above now reach the console by default**, where the previous file-only logger printed nothing at all; `ROLEBOX_LOG_CONSOLE_LEVEL=error` (or `fatal`) restores a quiet console. And there is **one file per channel** — `graph:host` writes `graph-host.log` — instead of a single `rolebox.log`, which is what keeps two processes from racing over one rotation; historical `rolebox.log` files are left exactly as they are, neither migrated nor read back as records nor deleted. `ROLEBOX_LOG_FILE=/path/to/rolebox.log` restores the single-file layout for every channel at once, rotation included. The variables are `ROLEBOX_LOG_LEVEL` (file threshold, default `info`), `ROLEBOX_LOG_CONSOLE_LEVEL` (console threshold, default `warn`), `ROLEBOX_LOG_LEVEL_<CHANNEL>` (one channel's threshold, e.g. `ROLEBOX_LOG_LEVEL_GRAPH_HOST=debug`), `ROLEBOX_LOG_DIR`, `ROLEBOX_LOG_MAX_BYTES` (rotation size, default 10 MB), `ROLEBOX_LOG_RETAIN` (rotated copies kept, default 3) and `ROLEBOX_LOG_FILE`. Details: [docs/logging.md](docs/logging.md).

### Features

- **Live log views react to source changes** — the log reader now watches the resolved file or directory and emits a debounced change signal. The dsh web panel and TUI Logs view refresh on that signal while retaining a fallback poll for platforms that do not report every append.

- **Logs are queryable, prunable and watchable — `rolebox logs`, a dsh web panel and a TUI view** — the same records are now readable back without `jq` archaeology. `rolebox logs` answers the newest 100 records and takes `--level`, `--channel`, `--code`, `--graph`, `--session`, `--text`, `--since`/`--until`, `--limit`, `--order` and `--json`, while `--follow` tails live; `rolebox logs files` lists every file's channel, rotation, size and modification time, and `rolebox logs prune` removes rotated copies under `--keep`/`--days`/`--max-total-bytes` gates without ever touching the file being written. The dsh web UI gains a right-Sidebar **Logs** tab that polls the read-only `GET /rolebox/logs` route (registered only when the host provides a web server), and the TUI sidebar gains a **Logs** view — `ctrl+l` opens it, `ctrl+p` pauses and resumes, `ctrl+up`/`ctrl+down` move the level threshold, `ctrl+n` cycles the channel filter and `ctrl+g` follows. Structured diagnostics also moved into a closed, typed event vocabulary (`src/log/registry.ts`): a registered code owns its level, its channel and its one-sentence m

releases.name: rolebox v1.10.0
releases.body:
### Features

- **Codex is a supported harness** — rolebox now targets Codex through a generated local plugin marketplace plus a rolebox MCP server: `rolebox sync codex` writes `<codexHome>/rolebox-marketplace` (the marketplace manifest plus `plugins/rolebox` carrying `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json` and a `skills` symlink to `<codexHome>/skills`), deploys installed roles to `<codexHome>/rolebox`, and registers one managed block in `<codexHome>/config.toml`, with the Codex home resolved from `$CODEX_HOME` when set and non-blank and `~/.codex` otherwise. The plugin starts the rolebox MCP server (`rolebox mcp`, also exported as `rolebox/codex`), a newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio server exposing 15 canonical tools — hashline_read/hashline_edit, memory_write/memory_recall/memory_list, web_search/web_read/web_fetch, asset_search/asset_inspect/asset_validate, reference_search, load_role_skill, signal and interactive_terminal — with no `session_*`, `dispatch_*`, `loop_*`, `task_*` or `graph_*` tools, no role switching, TUI, hot reload, extension loader or hooks-driven activation; the generated layout, the MCP protocol surface and those non-goals are documented in [docs/codex.md](docs/codex.md).

- **dsh roles reload in-process, without a restart** (ce96f44) — `POST /rolebox/reload` (served by the dsh role-switch route, with the monitor panel's "Reload roles" control as its entry point) performs an in-process, non-destructive role reload: roles are re-discovered and re-resolved into the live containers in place and the agent catalog is re-synced, so installing or editing a role no longer needs a host restart. Because consumers capture the resolved-role snapshot by reference, the four role-snapshot tools (`asset_search`, `asset_inspect`, `asset_validate`, `reference_search`) are rebuilt as one disposable generation and the lazy skill catalog is invalidated, while discovery and resolution run against local containers and every post-swap mutation is guarded by an in-memory rollback — a failed reload leaves the previous roles, role functions and open-role registry in place, so no partially swapped state is observable.

### Bug Fixes

- **Dispatch teardown always releases its resources** — `DispatchManager.dispose()` now runs its release tail in a `finally`, so a throwing state flush can no longer leave the watchdog timers running or the state lock held. Pending debounced progress writes are flushed and their timers cleared on teardown, so no write can fire after a manager is disposed.

- **Dispatch health is config-aware** — a stopped budget sampler now reads as a stopped pipeline only when a budget limit is actually configured, so a manager with no configured limits no longer reports unhealthy merely because its sampler was never armed, and a manager with configured limits no longer reports healthy while its sampler is dead.

- **Process-fatal events are recorded without changing host behaviour** — a new observation-only reporter flushes rolebox state and writes one structured log entry on `uncaughtException` / `unhandledRejection`. It never exits, re-throws, or alters the host's exit code, installs and removes exactly its own process listeners, and reports at most one event per process.

- **Graph Engine v2 correctness fixes** (7a7c67e) — Persistence DTOs are derived from the runtime types and validated per node, so a partial node state can no longer load as valid and silently disable the `max_total_*` budget gates after recovery; join quorum is a discriminated union that carries its count instead of a quantity-free member each consumer read differently; a dispatch kickoff that contends for the advancing lock is deferred and replayed instead of dropped, so a graph cannot sit in `executing` with no work in flight; `on_condition` loop-backs consume a traversal, which makes `max_traversals` enforceable for that shape; and the approval payload is serialized before the node is marked complete, so an unserializable payload can n
